in_hebrew.name: טרופימוס
in_hebrew.meaning: המשמעות היא מזון או חיית מחמד
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם טרופימוס נגזר מהמילה היוונית τροφίμος (trophimos), שפירושה מזון או חיית מחמד. השם משמש גם בברית החדשה של הנוצרים, בספר מעשי השליחים, כשהשליח פאולוס מזכיר את טרופימוס כאחד מתלמידיו. השם משקף את חשיבות הדאגה והטיפול באחרים, כמו גם את התפקיד של המנהיגים הרוחניים כספקי רוחניים לקהילותיהם.

in_greek.name: Τρόφιμος
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Τρόφιμος προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη τροφίμος (trophimos), που σημαίνει αυτό που τρέφεται ή εκτρέφεται. Στο Καινόν Διαθήκη, ο Τρόφιμος αναφέρεται στα Ακρά της Ασίας, όπου ο Απόστολος Παύλος συνόδευσε τον Τίχο και τον Τρόφιμο στην Ιερουσαλήμ. Ο Τρόφιμος συμβολίζει τη σχέση μεταξύ του πνευματικού οδηγού και των οπαδών του, καθως και την ευθύνη του πρώτου για την πνευματική τροφή των δεύτερων.

in_latin.name: Trophimus
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Trophimus comes from the Greek word τροφίμος (trophimos), meaning one who is nourished or brought up. In the early Christian Church, Trophimus was known as a companion of Saint Paul, mentioned in the Acts of the Apostles. The name reflects the role of spiritual leaders as nourishers of their flock, as well as the importance of guidance and care in Christian communities.

in_english.name: Trophimus
in_english.meaning: Nourished or brought up; a person fed or cared for
in_english.long_meaning: The name Trophimus originates from the Greek word τροφίμος (trophimos), meaning one who is nourished or brought up. In Christian tradition, Trophimus is mentioned in the New Testament as a companion of Saint Paul, specifically in Acts 20:4 and 2 Timothy 4:20. The name symbolizes spiritual nourishment and care, reflecting the role of leaders in providing guidance and support to their communities. Historically, the name has been used in various Christian cultures, signifying a connection to the early Christian church and its values.

data.cultural_impact: In ancient cultures, names were often indicative of family lineage, social status, or personal characteristics. However, with the advent of Christianity, religious meanings became more prominent. The name Trophimus reflects the early Christian community's strong emphasis on spiritual growth and divine support—an important value during a time when following the new faith could be risky.
data.spiritual_significance: In Acts 21:29, Trophimus is singled out from Paul's traveling companions and falsely accused of disturbing the peace in the assembling crowd at the Temple. The name's attachment to the early Christian movement shows that even in times of persecution, believers like Trophimus continued to nurture their faith and represent God's love. It is a reminder that, no matter the circumstances, one's spiritual nourishment and support come ultimately from God.

historical_references.reference: Trophimus of Ephesus was a Christian and a close friend of Paul who accompanied him on several of his missionary journeys. According to the New Testament book of Acts (21:1-18), Paul left Ephesus with Trophimus and Gaius to visit Jerusalem in AD 57. During this visit, Paul was arrested and taken before the Sanhedrin, but Trophimus remained in Jerusalem and was later delivered from a plot to kill him by Paul's nephew, Luke.

Trophimus of Constantina was a bishop and martyr who lived during the late Roman Empire, likely in the 4th century AD. He is known for his association with St. Martin of Tours, who allegedly built a church in Constantina in Trophimus' honor. According to legend, Trophimus came to Gaul as a missionary, converted St. Martin, and later became bishop of the city of Le Mans. He was martyred during the persecutions of Diocletian and his successors.
historical_references.context: Christian martyrs, association with St. Martin of Tours
